headline: Russia and Ukraine strike vessels in Black Sea and Sea of Azov
summary: Missile and drone attacks on vital grain export routes have triggered a rise in global wheat prices.
details: Ukraine and Russia launched missile and drone attacks on vessels in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, escalating hostilities in a zone critical for global grain exports.
Ukraine's military reported striking six Russian tankers and two tugboats, while Russia's defence ministry claimed to have hit a maritime vessel and a speedboat of the Ukrainian armed forces.
Russian forces also targeted several military and industrial sites, as well as deepwater Black Sea ports in the Greater Odesa area, which are essential to Ukraine's wartime economy.
The attacks have forced Russia, the world's top grain exporter, to limit shipping in the Sea of Azov, a route that handles approximately a quarter of of its grain exports.
Officials reported that five people were killed on both sides of the war border during these recent strikes.
Separately, large protests erupted in several Ukrainian cities, including Kyiv, where over a thousand people gathered to protest the removal of popular Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.
Fedorov, appointed six months ago, was seen as a military moderniser. His removal has caused uncertainty within the army at a time when Ukraine has been making strategic gains.

headline_marked: Rain-fuelled [[fruit fly attacks devastate Fazli mango harvest]] in Chapainawabganj
headline: Rain-fuelled fruit fly attacks devastate Fazli mango harvest in Chapainawabganj
summary: Prolonged rainfall has led to a surge in fruit fly infestations, causing large quantities of mangoes to rot on trees and resulting in heavy financial losses for farmers.
details: Prolonged rainfall in Chapainawabganj has triggered a sharp rise in fruit fly infestations, causing iconic Fazli mangoes to rot on the trees or fall and rot on the ground.
One farmer, Abdul Awal, reported that he expected 40,000 kg of mangoes but managed to collect only 8,000 kg of high-quality fruit due to the pest attack.
Awal stated that the flies puncture the skin of the fruit, leading to rot that makes the mangoes unsellable in the market.
Other late-season varieties like Ashwina and Bari-4 are also vulnerable to these attacks once the rains begin after June.
The Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) in Chapainawabganj suggests that bagging fruits is the most effective long-term solution to protect mangoes and improve their appearance.
The DAE also recommends the use of pheromone traps to attract and trap male fruit flies, reducing their breeding and lowering infestation levels.
Mangoes are cultivated on 37,487 hectares of land in Chapainawabganj this year, with a production target of 458,000 tonnes valued at approximately Tk 5,000 crore.
caption:
Rain-fuelled fruit fly attacks are destroying Fazli mangoes in Chapainawabganj, leaving farmers with massive financial losses.

Prolonged rainfall in Chapainawabganj has triggered a sharp rise in fruit fly infestations, causing iconic Fazli mangoes to rot on the trees or fall and rot on the ground.

One farmer, Abdul Awal, reported that he expected 40,000 kg of mangoes but managed to collect only 8,000 kg of high-quality fruit due to the pest attack.

Awal stated that the flies puncture the skin of the fruit, leading to rot that makes the mangoes unsellable in the market.

Other late-season varieties like Ashwina and Bari-4 are also vulnerable to these attacks once the rains begin after June.

The Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) in Chapainawabganj suggests that bagging fruits is the most effective long-term solution to protect mangoes and improve their appearance.

The DAE also recommends the use of pheromone traps to attract and trap male fruit flies, reducing their breeding and lowering infestation levels.

Mangoes are cultivated on 37,487 hectares of land in Chapainawabganj this year, with a production target of 458,000 tonnes valued at approximately Tk 5,000 crore.
